research.source: Gulzar, Zhu, Han, ‘Perception and Practices of Differential Testing,’ ICSE-SEIP 2019, DOI 10.1109/ICSE-SEIP.2019.00016
research.locator: https://people.cs.vt.edu/~gulzar/assets/pdf/p71-gulzar.pdf (published conference paper; PDF opened; pp. 71–72 / lines 29–44, 95–103, 144–168)
research.status_support: Original empirical practice study: survey of 117 engineers across 100+ teams, five interviews, and analysis of 2,104 diff tests. Reports differential testing supplements unit tests and helps examine preserved behavior where a full oracle is unavailable; also reports noisy/flaky outcomes, substantial run/differencing cost, and sampling/differencing challenges.
research.applicability_limit: Large Google-specific end-to-end practice study, not a controlled comparison of these tiny local regressions or a correctness guarantee. Differential disagreement flags a candidate; it cannot choose the correct provider/version, and agreement does not prove correctness.
research.decision_use: R01–R03: retain exact expected-contract assertions and narrow fixtures first. A matched baseline/current or C++/Rust comparison is supplementary when the same operation, bytes, executable/package, provider marker, and environment can be recorded. Preserve IDs, stdout bytes, exit status, and identity in the comparison.

research.source: Graves et al., ‘An Empirical Study of Regression Test Selection Techniques,’ ACM TOSEM 10(2), 2001
research.status_support: Original empirical study compares selection costs and fault detection across program versions. Safe selection retained all fault-revealing tests while selecting 60% of tests at the median, but sometimes could not reduce the suite; results were sensitive to program, change, and suite composition. Cost model did not directly measure selection-analysis cost and simplified heterogeneous costs.
research.applicability_limit: Older subjects/techniques and synthetic fault-revealing datasets; evidence supports conditional trade-offs, not a universal selection rule or a quota for this repository.
research.decision_use: Use source-linked local fixtures and actual reported contract as first discriminators. Consider systematic broader selection/generation only if exact fixtures fail to separate plausible causes, repeated similar cases justify its setup cost, or neighboring-path coverage is material; do not prune required acceptance based on historical averages.

research.source: Di Nardo, Alshahwan, Briand, Labiche, ‘Coverage-based regression test case selection, minimization and prioritization: A case study on an industrial system,’ STVR 25(4), 2015, DOI 10.1002/stvr.1572
research.locator: https://pure.ul.ie/en/publications/coverage-based-regression-test-case-selection-minimization-and-pr/ (university publication record and abstract; full paper not opened)
research.status_support: Published industrial case study with real regression faults. University record says test selection saved under 2% execution cost in that system; fine-grained minimization saved up to 79.5% while retaining fault detection above 70%, a trade-off; modification-informed prioritization did not significantly improve fault detection.
research.applicability_limit: Abstract/record only here; results are from one industrial system, and minimization allowed a detection loss. Not a basis for dropping cases under this task's fixed acceptance.
research.decision_use: Counterweight to assuming more systematic selection pays off: for R01–R03's few fast core fixtures, select the direct discriminator by source path and preserve all contract checks.

contrary_and_rejected: A baseline-vs-current or C++-vs-Rust diff is not proof of correctness: either side may be wrong, provider identity may differ, or output comparison may be noisy. Keep expected contract and identity as independent checks (L1).

Systematic generation can reveal interactions outside a minimized example, but literature does not show universal payoff; study effects depend on change and suite composition, and added selection/differencing costs can dominate small suites (L1–L3).
L3 is abstract/record-only, not full-text-verified; its reported minimization trade-off is expressly inapplicable to reducing this task's required coverage.
No evidence supports a preferred diagnosis, common cause among R01–R03, or a claim that any registered test passed.
